title: spec(ui): a page element dataSource can name an API endpoint (provider: 'api'), so a product page composes from a control-plane summary in metadata instead of a product-specific React widget (maintainer ruling 2026-10-12)
body:
Filing gate: a maintainer ruling in chat, 2026-10-12 (「现在转向」): cloud's pages stay metadata, objectui ships only product-agnostic blocks, and no new `cloud:*` widgets are added. Filed from the cloud maintainer's session. ⛔ Not a claim.

## The gap

`ElementDataSourceSchema` (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts`, the block around L236–300) binds a page element to an OBJECT: `object`, `view`, `filter`, `limit`. A control-plane summary such as cloud's `GET /api/v1/cloud/home` (plan, AI seats, storage, checklist flags, environments with their marketplace installs) is not an object, so a cloud page could not reach it, and every such need became a cloud-specific React widget in objectui: `cloud:onboarding-next`, `cloud:plan-status`, `cloud:workspace-timezone-notice`, `cloud:ai-model-status`, and the queued `cloud:home`. Their copy lives in objectui's bundles, so a cloud wording change is an objectui PR and a pin bump.

The renderer already has the adapter: `@object-ui/core`'s `ApiDataSource` (`provider: 'api'`, `HttpRequest` read/write configs carried in `ViewData`), the one the approvals UI rebuild on the standard renderer uses (objectui#2763). The contract has no door to it from a page element.

## Ruling

- `dataSource` gains a second shape beside the object one: `{ provider: 'api', read: { url, method? }, path? }`. `url` is a same-origin API path (the renderer promotes `apiBase` the way it does for `url` actions); `path` is an optional dotted path selecting the sub-tree of the `{ success, data }` envelope the element binds, e.g. `data.environments`.
- Element templates read the bound value through the existing expression holes and the `visibleWhen` `data` binding; a list-shaped block iterates it; a scalar block (stat, usage bar) reads fields.
- Same-origin only. No credentials in metadata; the console's authenticated fetch is reused. A cross-origin `url` is refused at parse with a migration-named message.
- Companion generic blocks (`stat`, `usage-bar`, `checklist`) are objectui#12197, re-scoped by the same ruling.

## Acceptance

1. Zod: both shapes parse; a cross-origin `url` is refused; `objectui validate` accepts a page that uses the `api` shape.
2. Docs: the page reference shows an `api` example beside the object one.
3. A cloud page (objectstack-ai/cloud#2777 part B) binds `GET /api/v1/cloud/home` with no cloud-specific React.

## Related
